answer_1.quote: We experiment on five target languages from four families, all of which have grammatical gender: French (FR), Italian (IT), Russian (RU), Hebrew (HE), and German (DE) ... The task is to improve gender translation accuracy for unambiguously gendered input sentences.
answer_1.outputs: target-language translations (sentences) generated by the NMT systems

answer_2.quote: Table 4 compares all models on the WinoMT benchmark using accuracy (Acc), ΔG, and our proposed ΔR metric ... BLEU scores ... are reported for generic test sets.

answer_4.quote: Fluent speakers of German, Italian, and Russian were asked to annotate the gender translation accuracy of a random subset of 100 unambiguously gendered sentences from WinoMT ... annotators were instructed to classify a translation with one of five discrete labels: masculine, feminine, inconsistent, ambiguous, and N/A ... Human quality evaluations ... were evaluated on a six-point Likert scale by two professional translators.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators classified each translation into gender categories (masculine, feminine, inconsistent, ambiguous, N/A); quality was rated on a six-point Likert scale.
